raw: | A test fails only on CI and never locally — e.g. `TestWatcherDebounce`: `expected 1 debounced message, got 2` | The test ASSUMED a timing premise instead of checking it. A debounce test needs the whole burst of writes to land inside the debounce window; each write resets the timer, so a gap larger than the window splits the burst and it debounces as two. On a loaded runner one gap between five `os.WriteFile` calls exceeded 500ms | `cmd/mxcli/tui/watcher.go` (`newWatcherDebounced`, the window is a field not a constant), `cmd/mxcli/tui/watcher_test.go` | **Get the observed value out of the CI log before theorising** — `gh run view <id> --log \| grep <test>`. I guessed "count 0, event delivery too slow" and built two controls for it; both passed, because the log said `got 2` and the real mechanism was the opposite one. Three fixes, each aimed at the measured failure: a window far longer than production (2s vs 500ms) so headroom is orders of magnitude rather than 2×; the premise **measured and skipped on** (`if burst >= debounce { t.Skip }`) so a machine too slow to emit a burst reports its own limitation instead of a product defect; and the message **polled for, not slept for**, so delivery latency cannot decide the outcome. The grace after the first message must be a FULL window — a split's second timer fires one window after the last write, so a shorter wait stops looking before the evidence arrives. Control the mechanism deterministically (100ms window, 150ms gaps → count 5) rather than trying to reproduce load, and verify the skip path actually fires (temporarily set the window to 1ns). This is the checklist item "tests don't rely on `time.Sleep` for synchronization" — the original even named the hazard in a comment without removing it. |
